title: Vishvamitra tries to take Kamadhenu
introduction: Vishvamitra tries to gain Kaamadhenu, but Sage Vashishta persistently refuses Vishvamitra's bargains and barters. 'When an ordinary cow alone is held sacred and it is an un-marketable commodity, how then can Shabala, a milker of any wish, be given away or bartered for other riches...' is the argument of Vashishta. Yet, Vishvamitra goes on his bidding, but in vain.
closing: If cow is held sacred in India it is held precious all over the world. Whatever is given by a cow, from its milk to cow-dung, it is put to use, even for medicinal purposes, which is evident from insulin and smallpox vaccines. Regarding go mahātmyam 'sacredness of cow' Bheeshma speaks at length about the sacredness of cow to Yudhishtar, in Anushaasanika Parva of Maha Bharata.
anena sakalavaidikakarmavidyājīvanādi karatvena atipāvitryena ca gavām atimāhatmyam gavām vikrayato paryāptavṛttikānām atyāśāniṣedhaḥ ca trayam api sūcitam - dk

havyam kavyam tarpaṇam śāntikarmayānam vāso vṛddhabālasya tuṣṭiḥ | svāhākāravaṣaṭkārau goṣu nityam pratiṣṭitau | gāvo yajñasya hi phalam goṣu yajñāḥ pratiṣṭitāḥ | gavām mūtrapurīṣasya nodvijeta kathamcana | na ca āsām māmsam aśnīyāt gavām puṣṭim tathāpnuyāt | nātaḥ parataram dānam nātaḥ puṇyataram phalam | tvacā lomnātha śṛngaiḥ vālaiḥ kṣīreṇa medasā | yajñam vahati sambhūya kimasya tadabhyadhikam tataḥ || mahābhārate ānuśāsanika parvāṇi yudhiṣṭaram prati bhīṣma uvāca :
evam śrutismṛtītihāsapurāṇādiṣu bahuprakāreṇa pratipādyamānam - go māhātmyam - vācāmagocaram iti dikpradarśanamātram kṛtvā - vasiṣṭaḥ - viramyate - dk

Here, on hinting in an indirect way about go māhātmyam 'the sacredness of the cow...' and its un-marketability, Sage Vashishta paused his negation, hoping that Vishvamitra will realise, as he is also well-versed in scriptures.
इति वाल्मीकिरामायणे आदिकाव्ये बालकाण्डे त्रिपंचाशः सर्गः
Thus, this is the 53rd chapter in Bala Kanda of Valmiki Ramayana, the First Epic poem of India.

verses.devanagari:
एवमुक्ता वसिष्ठेन शबला शत्रुसूदन |
विदधे कामधुक्कामान् यस्य यस्येप्सितं यथा
verses.iast:
evam uktā vasiṣṭhena śabalā śatru sūdana |
vidadhe kāmadhuk kāmān yasya yasya īpsitam yathā
verses.translation: "Oh, enemy-chastener Rama, when the Divine Cow Shabala is spoken in this way by Sage Vashishta, then that milker bestowed each and every fancy, fancied by each and every fancier, according to one's own fancy." Thus Sage Shataananda continued the legend of Shabala or Kaamadhenu, as a part of the legend of Vishvamitra to Rama and others.

glosses.meaning: by Vashishta, this way, [she who is] spoken to
cow with amazing coloured skin - Shabala
whose, whose, as to how, fancied

verses.devanagari:
इक्षून्मधूंस्तथा लाजान् मैरेयांश्च वरासवान् |

verses.iast:
ikṣūn madhūn tathā lājān maireyān ca vara āsavān |
pānāni ca mahāar.hhāṇi bhakṣyān ca ucca avacān tathā

glosses.meaning: sugar-cane [and its dishes,] honey [and its dishes,] like that, cornflakes, [rice-flakes etc.,]
arracks [Arabic 'arak 'sweat', 'arak al-tamr 'alcoholic spirit from dates in Arabia, and from sugar-cane and rice in India,] also
highly [very,] apposite to [royalties and army-men,] drinks, further

verses.devanagari:

मृष्टान्नानि च सूपाश्च दधिकुल्यास्तथैव च
नानास्वादुरसानां च खाण्डवानां [षाडवानां] तथैव च |
भाजनानि [भोजनानि] सुपूर्णानि गौडानि च सहस्रशः
verses.iast:
uṣṇa āḍhyasya odanasya api rāśayaḥ parvatopamāḥ |
mṛṣṭa annāni ca sūpāḥ ca dadhi kulyāḥ tathaiva ca
nānā svādu rasānām ca khāṇḍavanām - ṣāḍabānām - tathaiva ca |
bhājanāni -bhojanāni - supūr.hṇāni gauḍāni ca sahasraśaḥ
verses.translation: There emerged mountainous stacks of steamy foodstuffs, palatable side-dishes and desserts of rice etc., also the dumplings of cooked pulses, like that the cascades of curds and the other milk products likes butter, ghee, cheese etc. Thousands of silver dishes and hollowware fully replete with daintily soft drinks, like that full with sugar-candy preparations, and with preparations that comprise all the six tastes have come up together with delectable foodstuffs made out of treacly dumplings of cane sugar.

glosses.meaning: mountain, similar, stacks - have come up
palatable, foodstuffs [side dishes, desserts of rice,] also
sugar-candies, [or, SaaDabaanaam = juices with six kinds of tastes]
[foodstuffs made from the] treacly dumplings of cane sugar, also

verses.devanagari:
सर्वमासीत् सुसंतुष्टं हृष्टपुष्टजनायुतम् |
विश्वामित्रबलं राम वसिष्ठेन सुतर्पितम्
verses.iast:
sarvam āsīt susantuṣṭam hṛṣṭa puṣṭa jana āyutam |
viśvāmitra balam rāma vasiṣṭhena sutarpitam
verses.translation: "Oh, Rama, all of the men in the forces of Vishvamitra, who are already rejoiced and regaled by the regular feasts accorded by their king Vishvamitra, are now comparatively well gladdened when feasted by Sage Vashishta, in which they rejoiced and regaled, for a good measure.

glosses.meaning: rejoiced, regaled, men, consisting, it became.

verses.devanagari:
विश्वामित्रोऽपि राजर्षिर्हृष्टपुष्टस्तदाभवत् |
सान्तःपुरवरो राजा सब्राह्मणपुरोहितः
verses.iast:
viśvāmitro api rājarṣiḥ hṛṣṭa puṣṭaḥ tadā abhavat |
sa antaḥ pura varo rājā sa brāhmaṇa purohitaḥ
verses.translation: "Partaking that feast together with the best royal ladies of palace chambers, and with the court-scholars and the court-priests even the king Vishvamitra, who by his nature is a kingly sage, became exultant and energetic.

glosses.meaning: with, palace, chamber's, best inmates [royal ladies]

verses.devanagari:
सामात्यो मंत्रिसहितः सभृत्यः पूजितस्तदा |
युक्तः परमहर्षेण वसिष्ठमिदमब्रवीत्
verses.iast:
sa amātyo mantri sahitaḥ sa bhṛtyaḥ pūjitaḥ tadā |
yuktaḥ parama harṣeṇa vasiṣṭham idam abravīt
verses.translation: "When honoured along with his advisers, ministers and attendants by way of receiving a royal banquet, king Vishvamitra then in high admiration spoke this to Vashishta.

glosses.meaning: one who is honoured - Vishvamitra by Vashishta

verses.devanagari:
पूजितोऽहं त्वया ब्रह्मन् पूजार्हेण सुसत्कृतः |
श्रूयतामभिधास्यामि वाक्यं वाक्यविशारद
verses.iast:
pūjito aham tvayā brahman pūja arheṇa susatkṛtaḥ |
śrūyatām abhidhāsyāmi vākyam vākya viśārada
verses.translation: " 'You showed me a generous hospitality whereby I am esteemed by an estimable sage like you, oh, expert in sententiousness, now I wish to say for myself to which you may please listen.

glosses.meaning: for esteem, meetly [sage of your like]
[a] word, I wish to tell - I say for myself

verses.devanagari:
गवां शतसहस्रेण दीयतां शबला मम |
रत्नं हि भगवन्नेतद्रत्नहारी च पार्थिवः
तस्मान्मे शबलां देहि ममैषा धर्मतो द्विज |
verses.iast:
gavām śata sahasreṇa dīyatām śabalā mama |
ratnam hi bhagavan etat ratna hārī ca pārthivaḥ
tasmāt me śabalām dehi mama eṣā dharmato dvija |
verses.translation: " 'Oh, godly sage, this Shabala may be given to me for a barter of a lakh, a hundred thousand, cows. Indeed this do-all cow is a treasure, and the kings are the gatherers of treasures. Therefore bestow this cow to me. As rule this cow also belongs to me.' Thus Vishvamitra said to Vashishta.

glosses.meaning: to me, Shabala [do-all cow,] may be given
this [cow,] as a rule, mine - belongs to me.

verses.devanagari:
एवमुक्तस्तु भगवान् वसिष्ठो मुनिसत्तमः
विश्वामित्रेण धर्मात्मा प्रत्युवाच महीपतिम् |
verses.iast:
evam uktaḥ tu bhagavān vasiṣṭho muni sattamaḥ
viśvāmitreṇa dharmātmā pratyuvāca mahīpatim |
verses.translation: "When Vishvamitra addressed him in that way, the reverential sage Vashishta, who is a virtue-souled eminent saint, on his part replied the king in this way.

glosses.meaning: that way, who is spoken to - Vashishta, on his part
reverential one, saint, the eminent, virtue-souled one
to the king, in turn, spoke - replied.

verses.devanagari:
नाहं शतसहस्रेण नापि कोटिशतैर्गवाम्
राजन् दास्यामि शबलां राशिभी रजतस्य वा |
verses.iast:
na aham śata sahasreṇa na api koṭi śataiḥ gavām
rājan dāsyāmi śabalām rāśibhī rajatasya vā |
verses.translation: " 'I cannot afford Shabala, neither by the barter of a hundred thousand cows, nor by hundreds of millions of cows, nor by lots and lots of silver, either.

glosses.meaning: by millions, hundreds of [of cows,] even

verses.devanagari:
न परित्यागमर्हेयं मत्सकाशादरिन्दम
शाश्वती शबला मह्यं कीर्तिरात्मवतो यथा |
verses.iast:
na parityāgam arhā iyam mat sakāśāt arindama
śāśvatī śabalā mahyam kīrtir ātmavato yathā |
verses.translation: " 'Abandoning her from my proximity is unmeet for her, oh, enemy-subjugator, you cannot even subjugate me terroristically and try to wean this cow away from me, as Shabala is everlastingly and inseparably mine, as with the everlasting and inseparable respectability of a self-respectful person.

verses.devanagari:
अस्यां हव्यं च कव्यं च प्राणयात्रा तथैव च
आयत्तमग्निहोत्रं च बलिर्होमस्तथैव च |
verses.iast:
asyām havyam ca kavyam ca prāṇa yātrā tathaiva ca
āyattam agni hotram ca baliḥ homaḥ tathaiva ca |
verses.translation: "This cow makes the journey of my life possible. Oblations to gods or manes, enkindling of Ritual-fire, religious sacrifices, homa-s, the sacred rituals conducted as darsha, paurNa maasi, all are dependent on her.

glosses.meaning: [my] life's, journey - cow which makes the journey of my life possible
sacrifices - which accords material for sacrifices

conducting sacred rituals of = "#B3003A"> homa-s [Oxford: hom, n. (also = "#B3003A"> homa ) 1 the soma plant, 2 the juice of this plant as a sacred drink of the Parsees, [Persian = "#B3003A"> hom, hum, Avestan = "#B3003A"> haoma]
in her [in cow,] take basis - dependant on her.

verses.devanagari:
स्वाहाकारवषट्कारौ विद्याश्च विविधास्तथा
आयत्तमत्र राजर्षे सर्वमेतन्न संशयः |
verses.iast:
svāhā kāra vaṣaṭ kārau vidyāḥ ca vividhāḥ tathā
āyattam atra rāja ṛṣe sarvam etan na saṃśayaḥ |
verses.translation: "This cow is the bedrock for everything in its entirety, and regarding diverse and numerous indoctrinations, and even for add-on syllabics like svaaha, vaSaT, they are all dependent on this cow, there is no doubt about it. [1-53-14b 15a]
notes: When the Fire-Ritual, or homa is conducted each pouring of fluid oblation or each dropping of solid oblation into Fire-Altar is associated with Vedic-hymns addressing the particular receiver-deity, annexed with syllabics like: svāhā, svāhā kārāḥ at the end of each chant like indrāya svāhā, indrāya idam na mama... varuṇāya svāhā, varuṇāya idam na mama... 'to Indra this is scarified, this is for Indra, not mine... to Rain-god this is sacrificed, this is for Rain-god, not mine...' So also the vaṣaṭ is annexed to the hymns addressed to manes. To learn Veda-s one shall be eligible to perform a Fire-ritual, and if Fire-ritual is performed, some basic Vedic hymns are to be learnt, and all this is a cyclic affair, requiring much paraphernalia. This cow supplies everything at wish, without a hassle, either to the teacher or to the taught.

glosses.meaning: swaahaa, syllabified utterances, vaSaT, add-on syllabics

verses.devanagari:
सर्वस्वमेतत्सत्येन मम तुष्टिकरी तथा
कारणैर्बहुभी राजन्न दास्ये शबलां तव |
verses.iast:
sarvasvam etat satyena mama tuṣṭi karī tathā
kāraṇaiḥ bahubhī rājan na dāsye śabalām tava |
verses.translation: " "In truth, this cow is everything to me and ever-gratifier, that way by so many reasons, oh, king, I cannot afford Shabala to you or to anyone." So said Vashishta to Vishvamitra.

glosses.meaning: Shabala, to you, not, I afford.

verses.devanagari:
वसिष्ठेनैवमुक्तस्तु विश्वामित्रोऽब्रवीत्तदा
संरब्धतरमत्यर्थं वाक्यं वाक्यविशारदः |
verses.iast:
vasiṣṭhena evam uktaḥ tu viśvāmitro abravīt tadā
saṃrabdhataram atyartham vākyam vākya viśāradaḥ |
verses.translation: Though Vashishta spoke thus Vishvamitra being an expert in sententiousness then spoke this sentence compellingly and argumentatively.

verses.devanagari:
हैरण्यकक्ष्याग्रैवेयान् सुवर्णांकुशभूषितान्
ददामि कुंजराणां ते सहस्राणि चतुर्दश |
verses.iast:
hairaṇya kakṣyā graiveyān suvarṇa aṅkuśa bhūṣitān
dadāmi kuñjarāṇām te sahasrāṇi catur daśa |
verses.translation: " 'I bestow upon you fourteen thousand elephants adorned with golden girdles, golden necklets and golden goads.

verses.devanagari:
हैरण्यानां रथानां च श्वेताश्वानां चतुर्युजाम्
ददामि ते शतान्यष्टौ किङ्किणीकविभूषितान् |
verses.iast:
hairaṇyānām rathānām ca śveta aśvānām catur yujām
dadāmi te śatāni aṣṭau kinkiṇīka vibhūṣitān |
verses.translation: " 'I will grant you eight hundred golden chariots whichever can be yoked on with four whitely-white horses trimmed up with the sets of tintinnabulating bells.

glosses.meaning: with very white, horses, four, to yoke on
set of tintinnabulating bells, trimmed up with

verses.devanagari:
हयानां देशजातानां कुलजानां महौजसाम् |
सहस्रमेकं दश च ददामि तव सुव्रत
verses.iast:
hayānām deśa jātānām kula jānām mahaujasām |
sahasram ekam daśa ca dadāmi tava suvrata
verses.translation: " 'I grant you, oh, superbly vowed sage, eleven thousand fleetly galloping horses of high pedigree born in best countries of best horse breeding. [1-53-19b, c]

glosses.meaning: in countries, born in [famous countries for best horse breeding]

verses.devanagari:
नानावर्णविभक्तानां वयःस्थानां तथैव च |
ददाम्येकां गवां कोटिं शबला दीयतां मम
verses.iast:
nānā varṇa vibhaktānām vayaḥsthānām tathaiva ca |
dadāmi ekām gavām koṭim śabalā dīyatām mama
verses.translation: " 'I award ten million diversely coloured and differently divisionalized cows, whichever of them will be came of age as milker, thereby, let this do-all cow Shabala be given to me.

glosses.meaning: to me, Shabala, may be given.

verses.devanagari:
यावदिच्छसि रत्नानि हिरण्यं वा द्विजोत्तम |
तावद्ददामि ते सर्वं दीयतां शबला मम
verses.iast:
yāvat icchasi ratnāni hiraṇyam vā dvijottama |
tāvat dadāmi te sarvam dīyatām śabalā mama
verses.translation: " 'Or, oh, eminent Brahman, if you yearn either for gems or gold, I gift that much of everything as much as you can yearn, let Shabala be given to me." Thus Vishvamitra entreated again.

verses.devanagari:
एवमुक्तस्तु भगवान् विश्वामित्रेण धीमता |
न दास्यामीति शबलां प्राह राजन् कथंचन
verses.iast:
evam uktaḥ tu bhagavān viśvāmitreṇa dhīmatā |
na dāsyāmi iti śabalām prāha rājan kathañcana
verses.translation: When the shrewd king Vishvamitra spoke to the reverential sage Vashishta, that sage has clearly said, 'whatever it is oh, king, I do not surrender Shabala, the cow.'

glosses.meaning: by shrewd [king,] Vishvamitra, thus, who is spoken

verses.devanagari:
एतदेव हि मे रत्नं एतदेव हि मे धनम् |
एतदेव हि सर्वस्वमेतदेव हि जीवितम्
verses.iast:
etadeva hi me ratnam etadeva hi me dhanam |
etadeva hi sarvasvam etadeva hi jīvitam
verses.translation: " 'Really this alone is my gemmy cow, thus I do not require your jewels or gems... truly, this alone is my treasure, thus I do not require your gilded chariots, horses or elephants... really, this alone is my everything, thus I need nothing from you... and actually, this alone is my alter-ego, thus you cannot separate me from myself.

glosses.meaning: this, alone, truly, for me, wealth [treasure]
this, alone, for me, everything, really

verses.devanagari:
दर्शश्च पौर्णमासश्च यज्ञाश्चैवाप्तदक्षिणाः |
एतदेव हि मे राजन् विविधाश्च क्रियास्तथा
verses.iast:
darśaḥ ca paurṇa māsaḥ ca yajñāḥ caiva āpta dakṣiṇāḥ |

verses.translation: " 'This alone is my darsha, puurNa maasa rituals, and like that this alone is all my Vedic-rituals with worthwhile donations and oh, king, this essentially is of service in diverse activities of mine.

verses.devanagari:

verses.translation: " 'Oh, king, all of my activities are instated in this cow, then wherefore a lot of palavering a bargain or barter? I do not give away this milker any wish." So said VashishtaT to Vishvamitra, and thus Sage Shataananda continued his narration of the legend of Sacred Cow.

glosses.meaning: by a lot of, palavering, what is [the us]
